en: n. an act of asking politely or formally for something; a thing that is asked for; vt. to ask for something politely or formally
ex: She made a request for a day off next week.
她申請下週休一天假。

en: n. a supply of something kept for future use; an area of land protected for wildlife; a quiet manner that hides your feelings; vt. to keep something for later or for a particular person
ex: I'd like to reserve a table for four at seven o'clock.
我想訂一張七點四人的桌位。

en: n. something that can be used to help achieve a goal, such as money, materials, or skills; (plural) a country's wealth in the form of minerals, land, or labor; the ability to find quick and clever ways of dealing with difficulties
ex: Water is one of our most precious natural resources.
水是我們最珍貴的自然資源之一。

en: n. something that is said, written or done as an answer to someone or something; a reaction to something that has happened
ex: We haven't received any response to our email yet.
我們的電子郵件至今還沒有收到任何回覆。

en: vt. to limit the size, amount or range of something; to prevent someone from doing what they want to do
ex: The city plans to restrict traffic in the center on weekends.
市府計畫在週末限制市中心的車輛通行。

en: vt. to let something become known that was previously secret; to allow something to be seen; n. the side of a window or door opening
ex: The investigation revealed that the company had lied.
調查揭露了該公司說謊。

en: n. a long narrow piece of cloth used for tying things or for decoration; a long narrow strip of material; vt. to decorate with ribbons; vi. to form long narrow strips
ex: She tied a red ribbon around the gift box.
她在禮盒上綁了一條紅色緞帶。

en: vt. to remove something unwanted from a place or person; to free someone from something unpleasant
ex: We need to get rid of these old newspapers.
我們得把這些舊報紙處理掉。

en: a. fully grown and developed, and ready to be eaten; (of a person) experienced or mature; ready for something to happen
ex: These peaches are ripe and ready to eat.
這些桃子熟了，可以吃了。

en: n. the possibility that something bad or unpleasant will happen; a person or thing likely to cause something bad; vt. to do something that might have a bad result; to put something valuable in danger
ex: Smoking increases the risk of heart disease.
吸菸會增加罹患心臟病的風險。

en: n. a deep, loud sound made by a lion or other animal; a loud noise made by a crowd or a machine; vi. to make a loud, deep sound; to shout loudly
ex: We heard the lion roar from across the valley.
我們聽見獅子的吼聲從山谷另一邊傳來。

en: n. a piece of meat that has been cooked in an oven; a social event where food is cooked; vt. to cook food in an oven or over a fire; to criticize someone in a humorous way; a. cooked in an oven
ex: We had roast chicken with potatoes for Sunday dinner.
我們週日晚餐吃了烤雞和馬鈴薯。

en: v. to take money or property from a person or place illegally; to take something important from someone
ex: Two men robbed the bank at gunpoint.
兩名男子持槍搶劫銀行。

en: n. a long loose piece of clothing that covers the whole body; clothing worn on formal occasions to show someone's position; v. to dress someone in a long loose garment
ex: He put on his robe and slippers after taking a shower.
他洗完澡後穿上睡袍和拖鞋。

en: n. the process of decaying; nonsense; vi. to be slowly destroyed by natural processes; to become weak; vt. to cause to decay
ex: The wooden floor began to rot after years of damp.
木地板在潮濕多年後開始腐朽。

en: adv. not exactly; about; in a way that is not smooth or even; in a violent or unkind way
ex: The trip will take roughly three hours.
這趟旅程大約需要三個小時。

en: n. the usual way of doing things; a regular series of actions or tasks; a. done regularly as a normal part of a job or process
ex: My morning routine includes a short walk and breakfast.
我的晨間例行事項包括散步和吃早餐。

en: n. a piece of thick material used to cover part of a floor; a small carpet; (informal) a toupee
ex: A soft rug lay in front of the fireplace.
壁爐前鋪著一塊柔軟的小地毯。

en: n. a piece of information that people are talking about but that may not be true; vt. to spread a story that may not be true
ex: There is a rumor that the company will close next year.
謠傳公司明年將關門。

en: n. a sudden quick movement; a time when people are in a hurry; a strong flow of water; vi. to move or do something very quickly; to rush into something without thinking
ex: Don't rush me; I need more time to decide.
別催我，我需要更多時間決定。

en: n. a reddish-brown substance that forms on iron when it is exposed to water and air; a decline in skill from lack of use; vi. to become covered with rust; to become weaker from lack of use
ex: The old bicycle was covered with rust.
那輛舊腳踏車滿是鏽斑。

en: n. the purpose or reason for something; the interests or benefit of a person or thing
ex: For goodness' sake, stop arguing and listen to me.
看在老天的份上，別吵了，聽我說。

en: n. a small round plate with a slightly raised edge, used for putting a cup on
ex: She placed the cup carefully on the saucer.
她小心地把杯子放在茶碟上。

en: n. a food made from minced meat and spices packed in a tube-shaped skin, usually eaten hot
ex: He had sausages and eggs for breakfast.
他早餐吃了香腸和蛋。

en: n. an amount of money that you have kept; the act of reducing the amount of money or time that you spend; a. helping to save money or time
ex: She spent all her savings on a trip around the world.
她把所有積蓄花在環遊世界的旅行上。

en: n. a piece of cloth worn around the neck or head, especially to keep warm; a type of joint used to join pieces of wood; vt. to wrap in a scarf
ex: She wrapped a wool scarf around her neck.
她在脖子上圍了一條羊毛圍巾。

en: vi. to separate and go in different directions; to be spread widely over an area; vt. to throw things in various directions; to cause people to go in different directions
ex: The crowd began to scatter when the rain started.
雨一開始下，人群就開始四散。

en: n. a person who has studied a subject at a high level, especially at a university; a student who has been given a scholarship; a person who learns
ex: The scholar spent thirty years studying ancient languages.
這位學者花了三十年研究古代語言。

en: a. connected with science or using the methods of science; using careful, organized methods
ex: The scientific method begins with careful observation.
科學方法從仔細觀察開始。

en: n. a person who studies science or works in a science field
ex: The scientist announced a breakthrough in cancer research.
這位科學家宣布癌症研究有了突破。

en: n. a tool for cutting paper or cloth, with two blades joined in the middle
ex: Can you pass me the scissors so I can cut this ribbon?
你可以把剪刀遞給我嗎？我要剪這條緞帶。

en: n. a person sent ahead to get information; a young member of the Scouts organization; vi. to search an area to find out information; vt. to search for something
ex: The scout reported that the enemy was approaching.
偵察兵回報敵人正在逼近。

en: n. a small metal object with a sharp point and a spiral groove, used to fasten things together; a propeller; vt. to fasten something with a screw; to twist something tightly
ex: He used a screwdriver to tighten the loose screw.
他用螺絲起子鎖緊鬆掉的螺絲。

en: vt. to clean something by rubbing it hard, often with a brush; to cancel something; n. an act of rubbing hard to clean; low bushes or trees growing in dry areas
ex: He scrubbed the floor until it was spotless.
他把地板刷洗到一塵不染。

en: n. a mark or device that confirms authenticity; a sea mammal with a thick coat that lives in cold water; a material that stops liquid or air from passing; vt. to close something firmly; to put an official mark on a document
ex: Please seal the envelope before you mail it.
寄出前請把信封封好。

en: n. protection of a place or a person from danger or crime; the state of feeling safe; a guard; something of value given as a guarantee of payment
ex: Airport security checked our bags carefully.
機場安檢人員仔細檢查了我們的行李。

en: n. one of the two periods that make up a school or university year
ex: She will graduate at the end of the spring semester.
她將在春季學期結束時畢業。

en: n. a person who is older or of higher rank than others; a student in the last year of high school or university; a. older; having a high rank
ex: He was promoted to senior manager last month.
他上個月被晉升為高階經理。

en: n. the act of separating or the state of being separated; a period of living apart from a husband or wife; a space or gap between two things
ex: The separation between the two rooms is a thin wall.
這兩間房間之間只隔著一道薄牆。

en: a. sexually attractive or exciting; (informal) exciting or interesting in a way that attracts attention
ex: The company launched a sexy new sports car.
那間公司推出了一款很吸睛的新跑車。
